title: The local universe
summary: Galaxies around the Milky Way: the Local Group, the Local Volume within ~11 Mpc where distances are measured one by one, and the redshift-distance universe beyond it, organised into groups, clusters, voids and the Laniakea supercluster.

concepts.label: Galaxy
concepts.description: A galaxy with a position (l, b), a distance and a luminosity.

children.label: Morphological type
children.description: Elliptical, lenticular, spiral (Sa–Sd), Magellanic, irregular; dwarfs (dSph, dIrr).

children.label: Luminosity
children.description: K-band (UNGC, a stellar-mass proxy) or V-band (McConnachie), in solar units.

children.label: Dwarf galaxy
children.description: Most galaxies here: satellites of the Milky Way and M31 and isolated dwarfs.

concepts.label: Distance
concepts.description: From the Sun, in kpc or Mpc (1 Mpc = 3.26 million light years).

children.label: Distance method
children.description: TRGB, Cepheids, SBF, Tully–Fisher, group membership, Hubble flow: each with its own typical error.

children.label: Redshift distance
children.description: cz / H0: a velocity, not a measured distance; peculiar velocities distort it (Virgo's finger of God).

concepts.label: Group and cluster
concepts.description: The Local Group, the M81 and Centaurus A groups, the Virgo, Fornax and Norma clusters.

children.label: Local Group
children.description: The Milky Way, M31, M33 and about 100 dwarfs within ~1.5 Mpc.

children.label: Local Void
children.description: The empty region next to the Local Sheet that pushes us away at ~260 km/s.

children.label: Laniakea Supercluster
children.description: Our supercluster, ~160 Mpc across, centred near the Great Attractor.

children.label: Zone of Avoidance
children.description: The sky behind the Milky Way's plane, where its dust and stars hide galaxies (|b| < 5°).
